title: Periplus descriptions file
description: The hand-written .periplus/descriptions.yaml beside the map: what a node or edge does, and where the reader read it, and what the project's words mean. A top-level key not named here is ignored with a warning, so a file written for a newer Periplus still loads.

nodes.description: Node id, as the map writes it, to its entry.

edges.description: Edge entries, each keyed by the edge's from, kind and to as the map writes them, so an entry survives a new map run while that edge is in it. periplus show prints an edge's entry under its row, and periplus find lists an edge whose text holds the words searched. periplus stamp, stale and undescribed read node entries only.

terms.description: Term name to its entry: what a word of the project means, and the things it names. periplus find prints a term whose words or old names the searched words hold as whole words, and adds its things to the results. A word in two entries has two meanings. periplus stale lists a term id the map no longer holds.

text.description: What the term means, in plain words.

words.description: The words people use for it; a phrase of several words matches when the searched words hold it in order.

ids.description: The node ids the term names, as the map writes them.

origin.description: Who said what the term means: person when a person said it, code when it was read from the code.

text.description: What the thing does, in plain words. Use the words that set it apart, and do not name the other meaning: periplus find matches every word.

fingerprint.description: Written by periplus stamp: the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the code the entry describes. periplus stale compares it with the code now.
